content.comment_body: Hello, I'm working with two similar circuit diagrams (CD1 and CD2) for logging data from analog inputs. When uploading CD1 from my PC to [product_name], the data log module is not present in the program on the device. The program can run, but data logging isn't possible. If I try to download the program from [product_name] back to the PC, I receive a "Layout restore error. Use the default layout." The data log module is also missing in the downloaded diagram. However, with CD2, everything functions as expected and data is saved correctly without any errors. Does anyone know what might be causing this issue?

It appears that there is some corruption in the CD1 file. The Data Log block is only labeled "L" by the software, instead of "L1" as seen in CD2. Why is that? Consider starting a support request and contacting [company_name] directly.
I'm not sure. The block name is assigned automatically when it's placed into the layout.
I didn't mean to suggest you made a mistake. It looks like a software bug. That's why I recommended opening a support request and contacting [company_name] for further assistance.

Hi, It seems your program CD1 is corrupt. I can download it to a [product_name] device with no issues. But when I upload it to [product_name] software from the device, I get an error (as shown in the picture). I copied your complete CD1 program except the data log block into a new [product_name] project and added L1 with inputs AM1 to AM4 for recording. That program then displays L1 at the datalog block and appears to work. However, it might still be corrupted, because placing the cursor on the [product_name] icon in the taskbar shows a change in the onboard analog input, which I've never seen before. I recommend re-creating the program from scratch. Every time I use the datalog block, it's shown as L1. Up to now, I've never encountered such a problem. Best of luck.

Good advice regarding [company_name]: Creating a new program is simplest. I think that's what the user did with CD2. However, the real question is: Why is there corruption in the CD1 program? It's not the first time programs have become corrupted. [company_name] needs to improve the software to eliminate such faults.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are experiencing corruption in a specific circuit diagram file (CD1) when using [product_name] software, resulting in the disappearance of the Data Log module after transfer and error messages when trying to revert the process. While a similar file (CD2) works fine, CD1 fails to retain logging functionality, and automatically assigned block names are inconsistent. Users highlight concerns with software reliability and point out the risk of undetected file corruption, as well as inadequate error reporting.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect reliable, error-free file transfers between [product_name] software and hardware, with no loss of blocks or modules, and want the software to either prevent such errors or provide clear feedback when they occur.
